\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کامیاب} (kāmyāb)}{کامیاب (kāmyāb)}]{\ur{کامیاب} (kāmyāb) — successful}

\label{lesson:UR-C381-kamyab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to occur to, then the Urdu for to get down to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کامیاب}}
\textbf{\ur{کامیاب}} — \emph{kāmyāb} — \textquotedblleft{}successful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{محنت} \ur{کرو} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{کامیاب} \ur{ہو} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum mehnat karo ge to kāmyāb ho ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you work hard, you will succeed.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کامیاب}} (\emph{kāmyāb}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kāmyāb}, \textquotedblleft{}attaining one's wish\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ur{کامیابی}}, \textquotedblleft{}success\textquotedblright{}, is built on it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāmyāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāmyāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum mehnat karo ge to kāmyāb ho ge.} — If you work hard, you will succeed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to occur to, then the Urdu for to get down to, then say \emph{kāmyāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کامیاب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Successful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کارنامہ} (kārnāmā)}{کارنامہ (kārnāmā)}]{\ur{کارنامہ} (kārnāmā) — a feat; an achievement}

\label{lesson:UR-C381-karnama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to get down to, then the Urdu for successful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کارنامہ}}
\textbf{\ur{کارنامہ}} — \emph{kārnāmā} — \textquotedblleft{}a feat; an achievement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{یہ} \ur{کیا} \ur{تو} \ur{بڑا} \ur{کارنامہ} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar us ne yih kiyā to baṛā kārnāmā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If she does this, it will be a great feat.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کارنامہ}} (\emph{kārnāmā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kārnāma}, \textquotedblleft{}a record of deeds\textquotedblright{}: \emph{kār}, \textquotedblleft{}a deed\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{nāma}, \textquotedblleft{}a writing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kārnāmā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kārnāmā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar us ne yih kiyā to baṛā kārnāmā ho gā.} — If she does this, it will be a great feat.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to get down to, then the Urdu for successful, then say \emph{kārnāmā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فخر} (fakhr)}{فخر (fakhr)}]{\ur{فخر} (fakhr) — pride (in someone)}

\label{lesson:UR-C381-fakhr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for successful, then the Urdu for a feat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فخر}}
\textbf{\ur{فخر}} — \emph{fakhr} — \textquotedblleft{}pride (in someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{جیتے} \ur{تو} \ur{ہمیں} \ur{تم} \ur{پر} \ur{فخر} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum jīte to hameṅ tum par fakhr ho gā.}
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\textbf{\ur{فخر}} (\emph{fakhr}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{fakhr}, \textquotedblleft{}glory, pride\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شاباش} (shābāsh)}{شاباش (shābāsh)}]{\ur{شاباش} (shābāsh) — well done!}

\label{lesson:UR-C381-shabash}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for pride, then the Urdu for a marvel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شاباش}}
\textbf{\ur{شاباش}} — \emph{shābāsh} — \textquotedblleft{}well done!\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{جیتے} \ur{تو} \ur{سب} \ur{تمہیں} \ur{شاباش} \ur{دیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum jīte to sab tumheṅ shābāsh deṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you win, everyone will say well done.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شاباش}} (\emph{shābāsh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{shād bāsh}, \textquotedblleft{}be happy\textquotedblright{}, run together into one cry of praise.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for pride, then the Urdu for a marvel, then say \emph{shābāsh} again
\end{itemize}
